simple.meaning: סְגֻלָּה (çᵉgullâh) appears 8 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Exodus, Deuteronomy, 1 Chronicles, Psalms, Ecclesiastes, and 1 more, beginning at Exodus 19:5. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, covenant, commandment, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סְגֻלָּה (H5459) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows סְגֻלָּה through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: סְגֻלָּה (çᵉgullâh) / H5459 is tracked through Exodus 19:5, Deuteronomy 7:6, Deuteronomy 14:2, Deuteronomy 26:18. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

definitions.full: H5459. segullah סְגֻלָּה noun feminine possession, property (on formation see Ba NB § 95 b Kö ii. 1, 168 ); — absolute ׳ס Exod 19:5 5 t.; construct סְגֻלַּת Eccl 2:8 ; suffix סְגֻלָּתוֺ Psa 135:4 ; — 1 valued property, peculiar treasure , which ׳י has chosen ( בחר ) and taken to himself; always of people of Israel, first Exod 19:5 (E; ᵐ5 λαὸς περιούσιος = Titus 2:14 ; 1Pet 2:9 λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν = περιποίησις Eph 1:14 compare Br MP 102 ; MA 52, 235); then ס ׳עַם Deut 7:6 ; 14:2 ; 26:18 ; later ׳ס alone, Mal 3:17 ; Psa 135:4 . 2 treasure (very late), of kings 1Chr 29:3 (gold and silver), Eccl 2:8 .
definitions.rootNote: feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to shut up;
